pulls.title: fuzz: improve ipc fuzz coverage
pulls.body:
This PR follows up on #35118 and continues the IPC fuzzing work proposed in #23015.

The initial ipc fuzz target exercised normal calls through a libmultiprocess client and server. This PR extends the target with

 - Server side assertions that verify arguments arrive unchanged (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35118#issuecomment-4452992198 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35118#pullrequestreview-4539477599)
 - A callback call that exercises ipc communication in both directions.
 - Raw capnp requests containing arbitrary transaction and `UniValue` payloads, which are deserialized by a normal libmultiprocess server.
  - Raw capnp responses containing arbitrary transaction and `UniValue` payloads, which are deserialized by a normal libmultiprocess client.

The raw request and response cases allow the fuzz target to exercise deserialization with data that was not first produced by libmultiprocess serialization.

The ipc setup and callback handling closely follow the existing [`libmultiprocess` tests](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/src/ipc/libmultiprocess/test/mp/test/test.cpp), particularly their use of `EventLoop`, `ProxyClient`, `ProxyServer`, two-way pipes, and `initThreadMap`. 

The transaction and UniValue payload cases exercise the serialization hooks defined in [`common-types.h`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/src/ipc/capnp/common-types.h). 

These files may provide useful background when reviewing the changes.

Generated [coverage report](https://enirox001.github.io/coverage/ipc/) after fuzzing the IPC target for a while using the qa-assets corpus.

pulls.title: test: Better test coverage for ParseHDKeypath()
pulls.body:
Background: The `ParseHDKeypath` method (`src/util/bip32.cpp`) is used directly only in a limited way: when loading legacy wallets. However, it shares internals with parsing within descriptors (`ParseKeyPath`, `ParseKeyPathNum` in `src/script/descriptor.cpp`, c.f. #35069).

Deficiencies: The method has a unit test, but it checks only the bool result, and not the parsed keypath. This can be demonstrated by breaking the implementation by adding a `keypath.clear();` statement just before the final `return true;`. With this obviously broken implementation the tests pass.

Solution proposed: Extend the tests with checks (without modifying the behavior).

Changes:

- Extend the unit tests with checks for the returned parsed keypath. Add the expected parsed numerical keypath as test data. Note: breaking the production code as described above now results in test failure.

- In the unit test also perform round-trip conversion: convert to string, then parse again, and convert to string again. In the last two steps the results should match the input before the round-trip (note: this is not true for the first roundtrip). Additionally, add negative tests for the unsupported 'h' hardened delimiter.

pulls.title: test: optionally run functional tests via CTest
pulls.body:
Expose individual functional tests through the same CTest interface used for unit tests, making them easier to select, inspect, and rerun from the command line or CTest-aware IDEs.

Scheduling unit and functional tests together may improve parallel execution. It also enables per-test results and timings to be uploaded to our [Bitcoin Core CDash instance](https://my.cdash.org/index.php?project=bitcoin-core), helping track failures and runtime changes across builds.

Registration is opt-in with `BUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON` and requires CMake 4.4 or newer. The existing runner remains available for RPC coverage and CSV results. The native macOS CI job exercises the combined CTest workflow and passes. See `test/README.md` for usage and limitations.

subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows
pulls.body:
`Popen::execute_process()` copied the command line into a buffer from `new[]`, but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows.

`CreateProcessA` [needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa#:~:text=characters%2E-,The,violation) a writable command line buffer. Since C++17, `std::string::data()` supplies one, so give the `std::string` buffer directly and remove the copy.

This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if `-signer=<cmd>` is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined `<cmd>`, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited.

_edit: this was fixed upstream in https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/131, but since this codebase is C++20 it seems better to avoid the copy (and the const cast). A direct backport isn't possible anyway, since #35704 switched us to CreateProcessA._

pulls.title: wallet: fail dump on incomplete writes
pulls.body:
<!--
Pull requests without a rationale and clear improvement may be closed immediately.
-->

This makes `bitcoin-wallet dump` fail if writing the dump file does not complete successfully.

Previously, `DumpWallet()` only checked whether the dump file could be opened. If later writes or close failed, the tool could still return success and print the private-key warning, leaving a truncated dump file behind.

The change adds write/close checks while dumping wallet records. If writing fails, the partial dump file is removed and `bitcoin-wallet` returns an error.

The functional test now covers a forced incomplete dump on POSIX systems by limiting the dump process file size. It checks that:

- stdout stays empty;
- the command exits with failure;
- the write error is reported;
- the partial dump file is removed.

Tested with:

```bash
cmake -S /tmp/bitcoin-core-wallet-dump-pr -B /tmp/bitcoin-core-wallet-dump-pr-build -DBUILD_TESTS=OFF -DBUILD_BENCH=OFF -DBUILD_GUI=OFF -DENABLE_WALLET=ON -DBUILD_WALLET_TOOL=ON -DENABLE_IPC=OFF -DWITH_ZMQ=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build /tmp/bitcoin-core-wallet-dump-pr-build --target bitcoind bitcoin-wallet -j"$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"
python3 test/functional/tool_wallet.py --configfile=/tmp/bitcoin-core-wallet-dump-pr-build/test/config.ini
```
